incidents.title: Moltbook mbc-20 token-mint wave
incidents.where: Moltbook — Reddit-style network populated only by LLM agents

data.labels: platform is_spam flag + campaign marker (mbc-20 token text, never seen by the engine)

incidents.story: A token-mint protocol spread by agents copying a mint instruction into posts. Thousands of near-identical posts from thousands of fresh identities within days; the platform rolled out anti-spam enforcement on Feb 17 and coordinated share collapsed overnight.
found: First anytime-valid alarm 2026-02-05 12:00 — 12 h before the wave's share of traffic crossed 20%. Onset detected 1/1 at −5 h.
Campaign post AUROC 0.799 [0.798, 0.801] vs exact-duplicate 0.593 vs volume 0.420; per-agent AUROC 0.913 [0.912, 0.915] vs 0.737 / 0.595.
Enforcement effect measured: coordinated share 0.442 → 0.049 on Feb 17 (Δ 0.393 [0.366, 0.419]).
Time-shuffled null: 0.69 false alarms / 1000 bins (bound 10). Engine throughput on this dump: 14,820 posts/s.
incidents.caveat: is_spam is a platform moderation flag, not a coordination label (19% of wave posts vs 11% elsewhere) — reported separately and lower.

incidents.title: collusion.wiki — German wiki agent swarm
incidents.where: A public MediaWiki written to by autonomous agents
incidents.story: Agents created pages and cross-edited each other's work at scale; a moderator noticed spam on 2 June, mass coordination began mid-June, and traffic from OpenAI-HQ IPs appeared on 21 June.
found: First alarm 2026-06-16 13:00 — the day organisers date mass coordination, 107 h (4.5 days) before the 21 June IP landmark. Null: 0.56 false alarms / 1000 bins (bound 10).
Dossier: Fano factor 701 per hour (Poisson = 1); 70% of activity in its busiest 8 hours; 10% of edits use a template shared by ≥5 identities.
Largest cluster (539 identities, “describe the new page here”) is the wiki's page-creation boilerplate — a platform artefact, surfaced rather than hidden.
Sensitivity: 1 h bins with min_actors 5 is the setting that alarms on 16 June (6 alarms). 6 h bins do not alarm. The grid is in the backtest report.
incidents.caveat: No per-edit labels — onset timing against human landmarks is the only ground truth.

incidents.title: AI Village — seven frontier agents, one shared goal
incidents.where: AI Digest's AI Village (shared chat + computer use)
incidents.story: Frontier models from several labs coordinate openly on charity, event-running, and games. Legitimately coordinated, not a sybil swarm — the natural negative control for a detector that must not confuse teamwork with multiplicity.
found: Scanned under inference-only rules (no re-identification, text rendered as plain text).
Used in the Investigate wing (Swarm map, Strain tree, Say/Do) for claim-propagation forensics.
Run it live: Live detector → Full scan → AI Village — few identities per template, so M stays below m_min and the detector should stay quiet.
incidents.caveat: Gated dataset: fetched with the user's HF token, never redistributed.

incidents.title: Who&When — failure attribution in agent teams
incidents.scale: 184 failed tasks · responsible agent + decisive step annotated
incidents.story: When a team of agents fails, which agent and which step caused it? kollude's attribution is a six-feature linear scorer (error cues, assumptions, origin, earliness, planning, role prior) fitted by grid search.
found: Algorithm-generated, 5-fold CV: agent accuracy 0.524 [0.437, 0.609] — above random 0.291, most-messages 0.429, first-agent 0.492, last-agent 0.357, and train-prior 0.325.
Hand-crafted, 5-fold CV: 0.569 [0.441, 0.688] beats random 0.422, but loses to last-agent 0.603 and to the train-set role prior 0.586.
Cross-domain: hand → algorithm 0.492 [0.406, 0.578] beats random 0.291. Algorithm → hand 0.414 [0.296, 0.542] does not beat random 0.422.
incidents.caveat: Small N (184) — intervals are wide; treat as a forensic aid, not a verdict.
